records.name: Helstrom
records.held_by: The Helstrom assembly of interior naheesh and tree-minders; a tribal levy keeps the guard
records.summary: Helstrom is the interior capital of Black Marsh, a great city that no invader has taken, on the river fork at the heart of the Hist forest. In 4E 201 a standing assembly of tribal elders and tree-minders runs it. It hosts the great Root Talk each Hist-Tsoko. Outsiders may enter on sufferance. The city's real danger is its own guard and alleys.

aliases.alias: The immortal capital of the Argonians

notes.text: Helstrom is one of Black Marsh's great cities, in the reputedly inhospitable middle of the province and many call it the immortal capital of the Argonians. It meets the Root Talk and is run by its own people, not by any distant government.

Helstrom was already active in the late First Era, during the Blackwater War. After the defeat at the Battle of Argonia in 1E 2811 the native armies retreated here. The Empire refused to follow and never besieged the city. In 1E 2836 the Argonians simply stopped fighting. In the Third Era it became an incorporated city-state, and villages were built around it. Umbriel's path in 4E 48 passed it by.

In 4E 201 Helstrom is intact and the least Imperialised city in the province. The state's formal seat is lodged here and largely ignored. The assembly of naheesh and tree-minders decides by consensus.

sources.title: The Archwardens' formal seat at Helstrom is EXTRAPOLATED (state §1, §10.2); only 'capital' in the Simulacrum is canon (Lore:Kingdom of Black Marsh)

notes.text: Overwhelmingly Argonian, drawn from the interior's exclusive breeds: Agaceph on tail-poled rafts, with Paatru and Naga visitors and a very small outsider presence of perhaps a few dozen, each there on a naheesh's word. The guard is a tribal levy answerable to the assembly, not to strangers.

Helstrom does not trade outward; it receives and redistributes, because the rivers all drain to it. Rootworm and raft traffic, the Panther River fork and pilgrimage to the Root Talk bring it goods. Its market traders sell Murkwood feathers, sap, eggs and river fish.

The Hist, above all. Helstrom's city tree and its tree-minders matter more than any office, and the Root Talk, the occasion at which the Hist's alignment becomes audible to all the tribes, is held here in the holy month Hist-Tsoko. Sithis is honoured quietly; the Nine have no temple.

Stilt and root-hollow houses of reed, mud and living wood, with no stone and no outward wall, because the marsh is the wall. Black Heart-Mud pools between the roots, the air is thick and warm and rafts and plank walks thread the districts.

The city's alleys are as dangerous as they are fine, and its guard has a bad name. The danger is social: the levy answers to no outsider, the assembly's politics run deep, and its members will not discuss the sour-spring cycle. Past the city every approach is deep swamp.
A stranger stranded on the approaches is pulled out by an Agaceph raftsman. The assembly will not speak of its sour spring in open session. Every naheesh in the interior travels to the Root Talk.

records.name: Korydon
records.held_by: A council of craft-guild elders of the Chime-Keepers
records.summary: Korydon is the principal Chime-Keeper town of the interior, on a ring of dry ground encircled by water between Helstrom and the southern lakes. Argonians resettled it after the Kothringi died out and kept its name. It is orderly, prosperous for the marsh and known for tin-and-copper chimes, metal-woven rope and shallow-draft boats.

notes.text: Korydon is a market town of about two dozen residents on a ring of dry ground surrounded by water, the chief of the Kothringi-named towns of the Ultherus country. The name is a Kothringi one, kept by the Argonians who moved in; no source describes the place itself.

notes.text: A Kothringi town until the Knahaten Flu (2E 560–603) emptied it. Argonians, immune to the flu, moved into the empty houses and kept the old name because it belonged to the place. Over the centuries they took up Kothringi habits that the Hist did not forbid. Nativists elsewhere in Black Marsh called them half-foreign.

In 4E 201 Korydon is the most orderly town in the interior, run by a council of guild elders, cold toward the Archwardens and warm toward Gideon. Its chimes ring from every eave and the elders strike the great chime at dawn and dusk.

About 22 residents, nearly all Argonian with a few mixed families: chime-smiths, rope-weavers, boat-wrights, a tin trader and the elders. A few families keep a stone cairn for the old Kothringi dead whose houses they took.

notes.text: It makes tuned chimes, metal-woven rope and shallow-draft sail-and-paddle boats and trades them up the channels to Helstrom, Truowa and Blackrose for tin, copper, sap and dragon's-tongue gathered in the swamp.

Sithis and the Hist. The chime-smiths also keep a small chime-hung shrine to Z'en, the god of toil that the Kothringi worshipped, as a habit they took over with the houses. The town's tree-minder tends a village tree where eggs are laid.

Stilt houses on stone footings, a Kothringi habit; chimes of tin and copper hung from every eave; a market square on the ring of ground; boats moored three deep in the surrounding channel. The air hums with metal.

The town itself is safe: its elders keep a watch and predators seldom cross its ring of water. Beyond the channel lie Ultherus swamp with its dragon's-tongue, Tumnatu hunters and deep-water predators.
A Kothringi cairn of beads lies under the oldest footings; one chime rings on a still night; the guild elders quarrel over who may tune the Hist-shrine chime; a boatwright needs rare Ultherus herbs.

records.name: Truowa
records.held_by: A merchant council allied to Lilmoth's
records.summary: Truowa is a small trading city on the south-east shore of Lake Ulaish, where the lake's waters meet the Nushara channels toward Lilmoth. A merchant council tied to Lilmoth's commerce runs it. It is the interior's lake harbour, richer than the villages around it and wary of the Archwardens.

notes.text: Truowa is a small city, on the scale of Falkreath, at the south-east edge of Lake Ulaish where the water runs out toward Lilmoth. It belongs to Lilmoth's trade: goods from the delta and the coast arrive here and go up the lake to the Helstrom country.

notes.text: No song names Truowa before its rise. It grew from a lake landing where interior goods met coast-bound boats; in the generations after Umbriel destroyed Lilmoth, traders who would not live under the successor state came here.

In 4E 201 a merchant council, copying Lilmoth's, runs the city, takes a toll on lake boats and keeps a harbour watch. It trades openly with the delta and the Lilmoth coast and is cool toward the Warden fort at Gysilla.

About 38 residents, mostly Argonian, with a few Imperial, Khajiit and Bosmer traders on the quay, come up the river from Lilmoth's coast. Council merchants, harbour watchmen, ferrymen, rice buyers and a tree-minder everyone knows.

notes.text: Rice, fish, sap, feathers and clay come down the lake; cloth, tin, tools and salt go back up. The harbour master charges a mooring toll and the council holds the deep-water quay on the lake.
The Hist grows in a small city tree. Sithis is kept privately. The foreign factors keep a shrine to Zenithar.
Stilt quays and warehouses on reed piles, rose-washed plaster on the merchants' houses in the Lilmoth manner, rafts and canoes at every landing and the lake spread flat and grey-green to the west.
Safe inside the harbour watch. Smuggling and tolls start quarrels on the quay; out on the lake there are slaughterfish in the deep water and rival boatmen.

A cargo of cloth has gone missing from the quay and each side blames the other; the council refuses Fort Gysilla's toll and the garrison has begun stopping Truowa boats; a Lilmoth trader wants a guard on the boat road to Helstrom.
